name: Tesuk

anatomy.part: left palm, heart of the open hand
right thumb tip, touching the knot of string

myth: Hesk wound every string the islands flew, and she kept count of each knot in her two hands. When Aun cut the string and the sky drifted off, she did not stop counting. She held her hands open at the pole so the knots would not slip, and she counts them still. Each knot is a fisherman, a child, a kite that flew too far. My grandmother said the count is wrong by one. Hesk knows which one. She will not say, because it is the knot Aun tied in his own string before he cut it. He is still out there, trying to be counted. Tavo laughs at her and cannot be bargained with. Sil looks for him in the same dark. Mend your net. Count your knots. Keep your palms open.
verse:
Hesk holds open hands
counting every knot cut loose
one knot still flies on
